newsitem.title: ITALY: Two Italy generals step down over Somalia scandal.
newsitem.headline: Two Italy generals step down over Somalia scandal.

text.p: Two generals who led Italian forces on a peacekeeping mission to Somalia resigned on Saturday over allegations that their troops tortured, sexually abused and killed unarmed Somalis.
The office of the Army Chief of Staff said General Bruno Loi and General Carmine Fiore had asked to be replaced "to ease and speed up the investigations underway" into the allegations.
The Army Chief of Staff "accepted the request in order to contribute with the maximum determination to the rapid clarification of this affair," a statement said.

In Bologna, Prime Minister Romano Prodi, who announced a full inquiry on Friday into the torture allegations by news magazine Panorama, hinted on Saturday there might be further developments in government efforts to investigate the scandal.
Prodi told reporters there would be "a solution in a short time". He gave no details, saying only: "You will see in the coming hours."

Graphic reports of alleged abuses by Italian troops on a 1992 U.S-led humanitarian mission to Somalia were published this week by the news magazine Panorama, shocking Italians and embarrassing the army.

The reports, which include purported sexual violence against a Somali woman and allegations that Italian soldiers killed unarmed civilians, spurred the government on Friday to set up a joint civilian and military commission to assess the scale and extent of "deviant behaviour" among the armed forces in Somalia.
Loi commanded Italian troops in Somalia until the end of August 1993, when he was replaced by Fiore, who then led the Italian forces until their withdrawal in early 1994.

Loi said in a statement he was very bitter about what he called a "defamatory campaign" but added: "I have decided to put myself at the full disposal of the Chief of Staff with the aim of easing and speeding up the work of the commission."

President Oscar Luigi Scalfaro has also called a meeting next Wednesday of Italy's Supreme Defence Council, a body rarely meets, to hear a report from defence chief Admiral Guido Venturoni on international missions by Italy's armed forces.

Panorama began reporting allegations last week by a former soldier of torture of Somalis and on Friday it carried fresh reports of alleged abuses, backed by photographs and interviews with two more former soldiers.
One series of photographs showed what Panorama said was the sadistic sexual assault of a young Somali woman at an Italian checkpoint on the road from Mogadishu to Balad in November 1993.

The photographs, taken by an ex-member of the elite Folgore paratroop division, appeared to show the woman tied by her ankles to an armoured car, in a state of undress and being violated with a military flare.
Another ex-soldier, former fusilier Benedetto Bertini, told Panorama he believed Italian troops had killed at least six unarmed Somali civilians near the Somali border with Ethiopia.

The Army Chief of Staff has called a meeting of all captains involved in the Somalia mission and on Friday suspended one non-commissioned officer recognisable in Panorama photographs as apparently holding electrical wires and bending over the body of a Somali lying on the ground.
The man was identified as Sergeant Valerio Ercole, who told Italian television he was not a torturer and had been using wires from a field telephone to scare a Somali into talking.
Ercole said he stopped when the man would not talk and he realised his action was not convincing.
